Maria Chen: Quick follow-up from the load test last night — during the 10k rps burst we started seeing ~10-15% of edge requests hit steady 502s for ~20s windows. Not a full outage but a noticeable wobble.
Vikram Patel: Thanks, can you paste the log snippet? were failures coming from upstream or our proxy?
Maria Chen: Logs show upstream 504s briefly, but the gateway responded 502s. Looks like we were timing out while streaming and then the proxy abort path returned 502. Snip: ```[edge-1234] 2026-03-22T03:12:45Z GET /v1/generate conn_id=abc123 upstream=timeout(60s) proxy_abort=stream_close status=502```
Ashley Jordan: Hm — streaming abort handler returns 502 today if the client stream is broken and upstream still produces. That code path predates adaptive throttling.
Joel Rivera: Right — we fold several failure modes into 502 in the frontdoor. Makes consumer debug harder and also affects retry logic.
Vikram Patel: Load test reproduced by toggling `ingress.session_throttle` to low limit?
Maria Chen: Yes, repro steps in the harness: step 3 reduces per-session token refills to 0.2/s which caused long queuing + some midstream backpressure.
Ashley Jordan: Proposed short-term: split abort responses so that downstream-client-abort -> 499-ish and upstream-timeout -> 504. Then change hedging to only trigger on 5xx upstream vs client abort. Low-risk patch.
Vikram Patel: Long-term thought: adaptive-reset-exchange — instead of hard abort we emit a up/down reset handshake to the client when we detect persistent backpressure and allow client to resume with resume-token. That avoids double-write side effects and gives better retry semantics.
Joel Rivera: The tricky part is state—we'd need a small per-session sidecar LRU for resume tokens + TTL. That's another stateful surface on the edge. Memory/cost tradeoff vs fewer end-to-end retries.
Ashley Jordan: Agreed. Also need to guard against stale resume tokens replaying side effects. We should only allow resume for idempotent paths or when upstream indicates it's side-effect-safe.
Maria Chen: Here's a sketch of an ingress policy (YAML) for adaptive-reset: ```ingress:
  session_resume:
    enabled: true
    ttl_seconds: 120
    max_entries_per_node: 10000
    allow_resume_for: ["/v1/generate","/v1/chat"]
    require_idempotency_header: false
```
Vikram Patel: That looks fine. For max_entries_per_node we should correlate with p95 session size. If average resume entry ~150 bytes, 10k entries ~1.5MB — cheap. But indexing & GC are CPU-sensitive.
Joel Rivera: Operationally we must add metrics: resume_attempts, resume_success, resume_reject_reason, resume_memory_pressure. Also a circuit-breaker when node resumestore > 80% capacity to fall back to hard aborts.
Ashley Jordan: On retry semantics: when we handshake a resume-token we MUST not trigger server-side hedging or duplicate upstream calls. Therefore the token exchange needs to include an upstream commit-id or kvcache checkpoint.
Maria Chen: +1. For rollout: short-term patch (split error classes) in next sprint. Medium-term (adaptive-reset) as an opt-in feature behind feature-flag for Dedicated clusters.
Vikram Patel: Action items: 1) Ashley to draft minimal error-class split PR (assign to eng-runtime). 2) Joel to draft resumestore design doc + cost estimates. 3) Maria to update load-test harness to simulate resume handshake.
Ashley Jordan: I'll open the PR by EOD with unit tests for abort -> 499 mapping and change to hedging rules. :+1:
Joel Rivera: I'll start the design doc, will ping security about replay risk.
Maria Chen: I added the harness issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/loadtest/issues/142 — contains the exact steps.
infra-bot: Deploy scheduled: `canary/edge-runtime v2.14.1` to prod-canary at 2026-03-23T10:00Z — watch for 502 trend.
Vikram Patel: One more note — change affects billing logs (we currently bill tokens until proxy abort). Need billing to be aware if resume reduces billed tokens on client side. I'll loop in finance.
Ashley Jordan: Good catch. I'll add a note in the PR template for billing + observability changes.
Maria Chen: Cool. If we see the canary go green we can schedule a gated rollout. Thanks all.
